platform: Omarchy 4.0.6-1, Hyprland 0.56.2, kernel 7.2.8-9-omarchy, x86_64, Quickshell 0.3.2.r7, Node v26.8.2
scope: Live desktop acceptance of the 0.3.1 candidate: Epic is read from the store catalog instead of the curated free-games feed, so a developer-run 100%-off promotion is listed; the Steam country setting becomes the shared Steam/Epic country setting and copies a legacy steamCountry value on first load. Portable checks, the live harness and the four-store panel were run; no preview or theme screenshots were retaken because no rendering changed.
install: Update from 0.3.0: the development checkout is symlinked at ~/.config/omarchy/plugins/salmun-nister.loot-drops, so committing the candidate and running `omarchy restart shell` loaded the new build. The live shell.json entry (amazonEnabled true, hideSeen true) and seen.json survived, and the panel listed Epic with the new developer giveaway. The migration was then exercised on the live entry: staged `"steamCountry": "DE"` with no `country`, restarted, and the widget wrote `"country": "DE"` while keeping the legacy key; the panel still listed the three free Epic games with the German country. The original entry was restored and the shell restarted, leaving no country key. Fresh installation, removal and marketplace flows were not repeated; this candidate does not change them.
commands: staged steamCountry=DE in shell.json; omarchy restart shell; read the entry back
restore the original shell.json entry; omarchy restart shell

results.detail: ./tests/run passed 54 tests, the real Qt qmllint pass and the helper checks. validate_plugin.py reports valid with no errors or warnings and an advisory review-required security section; release_preflight.py reports READY with advisory matches only (QML process/network access and collected input, installer wording, and agent-instruction files in the tree); omarchy plugin validate . exits 0. These are limited scans, not a security audit.

results.check: Epic lists a developer giveaway from the live store
results.detail: The live panel's Epic Games section showed Agent A: A puzzle in disguise, GetHigh.EXE and Bad Cheese. GetHigh.EXE is the developer-run promotion from store.epicgames.com/p/gethighexe-c83d1f that the previous freeGamesPromotions source never returned; the row linked to that page and carried its 2 November 2026 end date. Hide-seen was toggled with v to reveal the acknowledged rows and then restored.

results.check: Shared country setting and legacy migration
results.detail: With no country key, Epic used its default and listed the same three games. Staging `"steamCountry": "DE"` and restarting made the widget copy the value into `"country": "DE"` while keeping `steamCountry` in the entry; the panel still listed the same three Epic games with the German country applied. Clearing the new key does not resurrect the old one (portable test). The entry was restored to its pre-test shape afterwards, so this machine stores no country.

results.check: Live harness builds and positions the panel
results.detail: ./tests/harness/run against the live stores reported 22 rows and laid-out content; the Epic bucket held the three games including GetHigh.EXE. This is the transport and layout check, not a substitute for the desktop pass above.

results.check: Existing settings and state survive the update
results.detail: The live entry kept amazonEnabled=true and hideSeen=true across each restart, and seen.json kept its Epic baseline and acknowledged ids, including the new GetHigh.EXE id. The temporary DE entry was removed afterwards and the shell restarted to the original state.

results.check: No preview or theme images changed
results.detail: This candidate changes the Epic source and a settings key, not rendering, so preview.png and the four theme images were left as captured for 0.3.0. The live panel was captured only as acceptance evidence and is not committed.

limitations: Live store contents vary, so a later fetch will not match the games named here. The Epic catalog filter (onSale plus the zero-price band) is undocumented and could change; the parser still requires a live zero-discount window, so a change would drop games rather than invent them. A non-ISO two-letter code such as UK or ZZ is passed through and surfaces as an Epic error rather than being guessed at. GOG's success path remains fixture-only because no giveaway was live. Installation, removal and marketplace flows were not repeated for this candidate. Amazon Luna's render is unchanged and was observed with its 15 live games. A vertical bar has not been observed. No security audit is claimed; the validators are limited scans.
